answer: Each identity locks bonded collateral in escrow, so a sybil swarm multiplies capital at risk rather than removing it. When evidence links k identities to coordinated equivocation, the correlated-pair penalty grows as O(k^2). Detection then triggers compounded forfeiture and asymmetric depreciation, creating an exponential multiplier in the swarm’s capital loss. A crystal-clear audit trail helps validators separate coordination from a tide of independent faults and makes it costly to forge identities.
